decisions.reason: As an extension of the firm's core trusted second-channel authentication offering, it likely remains inexpensive to maintain and strategically useful, so management would keep it even though several years of limited visibility raise some risk of later consolidation.

Mobile PDF signing still fits the firm's move toward secure digital contracting and cross-channel identity services, but after four years the option value is lower and a withdrawal becomes more plausible if adoption has remained modest.

A multi-layer end-to-end security architecture is central to the firm's technical base and broader platform logic, so even if marketed less prominently it is more likely to be retained as a core capability than abandoned.

After several years, a payment-network compliance suite that is less central to the firm's main identity-and-mobile-security trajectory and not visibly prominent is likely to have revealed limited standalone upside, making resource redeployment the better choice.
